title: I plow highways on the night shift. Dispatch just asked who's riding in my truck.
story:
"Unit nine, who's that in the cab with you?" I looked over. Dale was staring out at the snow, same as he had all night.

Dale rides along on bad nights. He never shuts up. Tonight he hadn't said one word since we left the yard. His coffee sat in the cup holder, still full, gone cold hours ago.

"It's Dale," I said into the radio.

The radio hissed for a long time. "Dale called in sick. He's home. I'm looking at your cab camera right now, and whoever that is… he hasn't blinked once."

I kept my eyes on the road. The wipers thudded. I could feel him beside me, not moving, and the cab kept getting colder, even with the heat on high.

Then, in the headlights, a man was standing in the middle of the highway, waving both arms. Orange coat. Gray beard. It was Dale. The real Dale, screaming something I couldn't hear.

My foot went to the brake.

And the thing in the passenger seat finally spoke, in Dale's voice, low and calm.

"Don't stop."
premise: a snowplow driver's silent ride-along partner is not his partner; dispatch says the real one is home, then the real one appears in the road and the passenger says don't stop
